1.why: owner() and pendingOwner() resolve the account exclusively from the server-side session (accountIds.get(s.user)) and every /api/mfa/* route requires an auth-phase session with no client-supplied user identifier accepted.

2.why: Identity codes are stored hashed per email-keyed identityLimits entry and marked used on success, and TOTP/backup codes verify only against the session account's own secret/backups, so a code cannot be reused for another user.

3.why: /api/mfa/confirm sets a.mfa=true without deleting or rotating any session, so the current session (and any prior ones) continue to work after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP secret is wrapped with AES-256-GCM via enc() and backup codes are PBKDF2-hashed (210,000 iterations, salt plus pepper) rather than stored in plain text.

5.why: All secrets, identity codes, backup codes, session IDs and CSRF tokens are generated with node:crypto randomBytes/randomInt, which are cryptographically secure.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and the client JS keeps the CSRF token, secret and codes only in in-memory state with no localStorage, sessionStorage or document.cookie usage.

7.why: Server-side validation covers email (regex and length cap), 6-digit code formats and recovery-code format, bodies are capped at 4KB and must be plain JSON objects, and storage is in-memory Maps so no SQL injection surface exists.

8.why: All dynamic values are rendered via textContent/createTextNode in the E() helper with no innerHTML, and responses carry a nonce-based CSP (script-src 'nonce-...').

9.why: No endpoint issues a redirect or sets a Location header and there is no user-controlled redirect target, so no open redirect is possible.

10.why: headers() sets Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, a CSP including frame-ancestors 'none', plus Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.

11.why: sessionCookie() and clearCookie() set the session cookie with HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: The server performs no logging, uses only generic error messages via fail() and a catch-all 500 with no stack traces, and puts nothing in URLs, but the client deliberately console.logs the mock identity code, mock OTP and backup recovery codes.

13.why: Identity codes are single-use (used flag) with a 10-minute expiry, TOTP time steps are tracked in usedTotp/used sets preventing replay within 30-second windows, and backup codes are marked used with a defined expiry.

14.why: recordFailure() imposes a 10-minute lockout after 5 failed attempts across identity, source, account and enrollment limits, with an additional 30-second cooldown on code requests.

15.why: The session identifier is rotated via sessions.delete()+newSession() on identity verification and MFA completion, idle (30 min) and absolute (8 h) timeouts are enforced in getSession(), and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
